faqs.question: What can I dress up as using only clothes I already own?
faqs.answer: Start from your strongest single garment and build four characters from it. A black turtleneck with dark trousers becomes a beatnik poet, a stagehand, a secret agent or a film director, each needing one extra piece such as sunglasses or a rolled-paper megaphone.

faqs.question: How fast can I put together a costume from stuff at home?
faqs.answer: Most ideas on this page take 5 to 20 minutes. The quickest are the bathroom and bedroom ones, such as the shower singer or sleepwalker at about 5 minutes; a white-sheet drape takes longest because it has to be pinned and tested.

faqs.question: Can I use acrylic or poster paint on my face for Halloween?
faqs.answer: No. Craft, poster and acrylic paints are made for paper and walls, not skin, so stick to cosmetics you already own. Even face paint can injure the eyes: a 2017 BMJ Case Reports account describes corneal damage after face paint was applied to both upper eyelids before a Halloween party.

faqs.question: Which Halloween looks need nothing but makeup?
faqs.answer: A raggedy doll, a bruised boxer, a silent-film star and a circus strongman all work with eyeliner, lipstick, blush and eyeshadow. Patch-test on your inner arm first and keep colour off the eyelids.

faqs.question: How do I ask a friend if I can borrow their costume?
faqs.answer: Ask seven or more days before 31 October, put your makeup on after you dress, and return it washed within 3 days. Hubbub's UK survey found 73% of people were happy to wear a used costume from a friend or relative, so the ask is rarely awkward.

faqs.question: How does a Halloween costume swap work?
faqs.answer: Each guest brings one or two costumes or pieces, and a one-in, one-out rule stops anyone leaving with a pile. Anything left unclaimed goes to a charity shop the following week rather than back into a cupboard.

faqs.question: How many Halloween costumes are thrown away each year?
faqs.answer: The charity Hubbub estimated 7 million a year in the UK, in its 2017 research, and found 2 in 5 costumes are worn only once. These are UK figures and several years old, so treat them as an order of magnitude.

faqs.question: Are shop-bought Halloween costumes mostly plastic?
faqs.answer: In the Fairyland Trust's 2019 survey of 324 Halloween clothing items from 19 retailers, 83% of the material was plastic-based and 69% was polyester. Its 2021 snapshot still found about three-quarters polyester.

faqs.question: Which household items make the best costume props?
faqs.answer: Objects with many possible uses work best: a colander becomes a helmet, red oven gloves become lobster claws, a net curtain becomes a beekeeper's veil and a cardboard box becomes a delivery bag. Psychologists call the habit of seeing only an object's normal job functional fixedness.

faqs.question: Can I send a photo of my homemade costume to someone as a Halloween greeting?
faqs.answer: Yes. SubhSandesh's Halloween card takes up to six photos, which the recipient uncovers by wiping fog off portraits, and it ends with a Boo License. It is a one-person page, not a party invitation.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Costumes Without Buying Anything, From Your Own Closet

Halloween costumes without buying anything start with one garment you already own, then borrow the rest from other rooms: a colander, a bath towel, the toolbox, the recycling bin. Below are 34 of them, sorted by where in your home the pieces live, including a one-garment matrix and four makeup-only looks.

Most people decide late. When SubhSandesh measured 89 Raksha Bandhan pages, the nearest festival data we hold, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself, so this list assumes you have one evening, not a week. Every idea also has to read in a phone photo, since 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages get opened on a phone, and a costume needing a two-minute explanation fails that test.

## What counts as a costume made without buying anything?

A zero-spend costume uses only things already inside your home, or borrowed from someone else's, with nothing fetched from a shop. Tape, safety pins and a marker count only if they are already in a drawer. In UK research by the environmental charity [Hubbub](https://hubbub.org.uk/sew-spooky), only 14% of Halloween costumes were home-made.

The hard part is seeing a household object as anything other than its normal job. Psychologists call that habit functional fixedness, and [Kroneisen and colleagues (2021)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7870631) argue that objects differ in how many non-standard uses they allow. Walk through each room asking what an object could be, not what it is for.

Indian readers already have a word for this. A [2025 pilot study of 20 Indian-born women](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12642356) describes jugaad as creative problem-solving under resource constraints, and found financial pressure predicted using it. Treat that as a small sample, not a law, but the instinct is the one this page asks you to use.

## 14 costumes from six rooms of your home

Each entry gives the costume, the pieces, the room they come from and an estimated time to dress. The wardrobe gets its own matrix in the next section.

### 1. The kitchen: colander, foil and oven gloves

- **Thought-reading inventor:** colander worn as a helmet, old charging cables threaded through the holes, a white shirt as a lab coat. 15 minutes.
- **Tin-foil-hat conspiracy theorist:** a foil cap shaped round a mixing bowl, red wool from the sewing box, a notebook of wild theories. 10 minutes.
- **Lobster:** red top and trousers, red oven gloves as claws, two pipe-cleaner or twist-tie antennae. 10 minutes.

### 2. The bathroom: towels and the shower cap

- **Spa escapee:** dressing gown, towel twisted into a turban, cucumber slices from the fridge carried in a dish. 5 minutes.
- **Shower singer:** shower cap, a loofah on a string, a shampoo bottle held as a microphone. 5 minutes.

### 3. The bedroom: pyjamas and the duvet

- **Sleepwalker:** pyjamas, an eye mask pushed up on the forehead, arms out in front, a teddy dangling from one hand. 5 minutes.
- **Burrito:** a beige or white blanket rolled round you as the tortilla, a green scarf and red top peeking out as the filling. 10 minutes.

### 4. The garage and toolbox: buckets, gloves and net

- **Window cleaner:** a bucket, a squeegee or dustpan brush, a cloth over one shoulder, wellies. 5 minutes.
- **Beekeeper:** white or pale clothes, gardening gloves, an old net curtain draped over a sun hat as the veil. 15 minutes.
- **Weekend handyman:** tool belt or apron, a tape measure clipped to the waistband, a pencil behind one ear. 5 minutes.

### 5. The kids' toy box: plush and plastic

- **Lost-property office:** six or more soft toys safety-pinned across a plain top, each with a paper tag reading FOUND and a date. 15 minutes.
- **Palaeontologist:** sun hat, a spare toothbrush as a fossil brush, toy dinosaurs half-buried in a shoebox of soil. 15 minutes.

### 6. The recycling bin: boxes and old newspapers

- **Takeaway delivery rider:** a big cardboard box on your back as the bag, a cycling helmet, a phone held up as if checking the map. 10 minutes.
- **Walking crossword:** newspaper crossword pages pinned over a plain top, a pen behind one ear, half the answers filled in wrong. 15 minutes.

## One garment, four costumes: the wardrobe matrix

If the closet holds only one strong piece, it still makes four characters once you add something from another room. The table compares four common garments by what they become, what they borrow and how long they take.

| Garment you own | 4 costumes it becomes | Borrowed from elsewhere | Est. minutes to dress |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black turtleneck and trousers | Beatnik poet, stagehand, secret agent, film director | Sunglasses, wired earphones as a headset, a coiled phone cable, a rolled-paper megaphone | 5–15 |
| Plain white flat sheet | Patient who wandered off the ward, marble statue, Lady Justice, Cupid | A paper wristband, talc for the statue's hair, kitchen scales, a toy bow | 10–20 |
| Striped top | Old-time prisoner, French onion seller, gondolier, football referee | A paper number, a string of onions, a broom as an oar, cereal-box red and yellow cards | 5–10 |
| Denim jacket or shirt | Mechanic, 1990s pop star, gold prospector, hitchhiker | A spanner, a second denim piece, a frying pan with foil nuggets, a cardboard sign | 5–15 |

The black turtleneck is the most flexible row, because every costume in it needs only one borrowed piece. The white sheet takes longest, since a drape has to be pinned and tested before it stays up through an evening.

## Makeup-only costumes, and why craft paint stays off skin

These four use only makeup you already own, plus whatever you are wearing. Eyeliner, lipstick, blush and eyeshadow do almost all of the work.

- **Raggedy doll:** round blush circles, eyeliner freckles, short lashes drawn under each eye.
- **Bruised boxer:** purple and yellow eyeshadow blended under one eye, a towel over your shoulders.
- **Silent-film star:** pale powder, dark lipstick in a small bow, heavy eyeliner, black and white clothes.
- **Circus strongman:** a curled handlebar moustache in eyebrow pencil, a vest, a broom held like a barbell.

Use cosmetics only, because craft, poster and acrylic paints are made for paper and walls, not skin. Even products sold as face paint can hurt near the eyes: a 2017 [BMJ Case Reports account](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5612553) describes a woman who painted both upper eyelids before a Halloween party and developed corneal injuries in both eyes, which took until day 4 to heal. Patch-test anything on your inner arm first, and keep colour off the eyelids.

## How to borrow or swap a costume without the awkwardness

Borrowing is the other zero-spend route, and most people are open to it. Hubbub's survey found 73% of people were happy to wear a used costume from a friend or relative.

The friction comes from timing, stains and late returns. Five rules keep the friendship intact.

- Ask seven or more days ahead of 31 October, never that afternoon.
- Never put makeup near a borrowed collar; dress first, then do your face.
- Return it washed, or as the label says, within 3 days.
- Point out any damage before you hand it back, and offer to fix or replace it.
- Lend something back the same week, even if it is only a hat.

For a swap, ask each guest to bring one or two items and use a one-in, one-out rule so nobody leaves with a pile. Whatever nobody claims goes to a charity shop the following week, not back into a cupboard.

## The waste you skip: 7 million costumes and 2,079 tonnes of plastic

Skipping the shop is about more than money, because most bought costumes have a short life. [Hubbub's Sew Spooky campaign](https://hubbub.org.uk/sew-spooky) estimates that 7 million Halloween costumes are thrown away in the UK each year (its 2017 figure), and that 2 in 5 costumes are worn only once.

The material makes it worse. A [2019 Fairyland Trust survey](https://www.fairylandtrust.org/the-scariest-thing-about-halloween-is-the-plastic-2019/) of 324 Halloween clothing items from 19 retailers found 83% of the material was plastic-based and 69% was polyester. Applied to 7 million discarded costumes, that is 2,079 tonnes of plastic, which the trust equates by weight to 83 million drinks bottles.

These are UK numbers and they are now several years old; we found no newer survey of the same scale. Read them as an order of magnitude, not a current count.

## One costume photo, one recipient: our Halloween card and its limits

A costume made from a colander and a bath towel is worth a photo, and that photo can go to one person who missed the night. On our [Halloween card with photos and music](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween), your costume shots sit in foggy portraits the recipient wipes clean, after they knock three times and carve the pumpkin. The final Boo License lets you assign them a costume too, one of eight, from ghost to bat.

Choose the partner, bestie, family or kids version to match who receives it; 90.9% of pages started on SubhSandesh end up published and shared. The [cinematic premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) holds 12 photos plus a 60-second voice note, if one costume shot is not enough.

Neither page plans a party or a group costume, and both serve a single recipient with an English interface. If that person stands next to you at the party, the costume itself is the greeting. Zero-spend dressing also loses to a bought or built costume when a school or office bans face coverings, or when a contest judges craftsmanship.

## Sources

- Hubbub, Sew Spooky campaign page, costume research from 2017 and 2019 (page undated).
- Fairyland Trust, "The Scariest Thing About Halloween Is the Plastic (2019)", 17 October 2019.
- Kroneisen, Kriechbaumer, Kamp and Erdfelder, Psychonomic Bulletin and Review, February 2021.
- Singh, BMC Women's Health, 24 November 2025.
- Ho, Ramessur and Webber, BMJ Case Reports, May 2017 (abstract read).

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the five pages analysed: it is the only one that organises zero-spend costumes by room and garment, and the only one with dated, sourced costume-waste figures (Hubbub 2017, Fairyland Trust 2019) and an eye-safety case report. Three of the top results are hijacked-subdomain spam and one is a 2017 news page, so the bar is low. Still, the waste numbers are UK-only and 7–9 years old, there is no first-party Halloween data, and a new domain will take months to compete with any authority site that targets this query.
